label: A particular valid demand requires both standing and legitimate content
definition: A specified demand that a claimant is entitled to address to a specified agent falls within that claimant's legitimate second-personal authority and gives the agent an accountability-grounded reason for compliance. It need not actually have been spoken or communicated. Generic membership or equal standing to make some claims does not determine which concrete demands fall within that authority.
note: Darwall pp. 7–9 distinguishes interdefined authority and valid demands, but pp. 9 and 15 ask what makes any demand valid. This definition leaves the content/jurisdiction application substantive and open.
